notes: Heat shock from 25 C to 50 C applied within 36 s (~33.3 C/min), followed by a 30 min plateau at 50 C; measured after recovery at 25 C. Value is the proportion of DiBAC4(3)-positive (depolarized) cells; the table header does not state the unit, but the text describes it as the proportion of cells with depolarized membranes. Unstressed control 2.39, boiled positive control 98.64 (neither emitted as a record).

notes: Heat slope regime: gradual heating from 25 C to 50 C at 0.5 C/min followed by a 30 min plateau at 50 C. temp_shift left null because the schema has no term for a gradual ramp. Proportion of DiBAC4(3)-positive (depolarized) cells; gradual heating causes far less depolarization than heat shock.

source_quote: the CBS1171 strain exhibits a higher level of cultivability after a heat shock at 50°C for 30 min in a binary water-sorbitol medium (Martinez de Marañon et al ., 1999 : ∼ 60%) than in PBS (present study: ∼ 22%)
notes: Cultivability (colony formation) after heat shock at 50 C for 30 min in PBS, i.e. without nutrients. Value is approximate (~22%) as stated in the Discussion; the corresponding figure (Fig. 1B) is the primary data. The ~60% figure in the same sentence is from a different study and is not extracted.
